checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.54pp larger on average (224 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: 'Variant arms are live in the arena' is green, listing 5 running arms including entry-8pct.
findings.problem: entry-8pct has live_n=5 and vol-4x has live_n=15 against a confirm plan of n=600, and entry-8pct's screen_n=498 with declined=79 means it sees a fraction of the shared stream. A green 'arms are live' box conflates registered-and-detecting with accumulating live evidence at a rate that could ever reach the confirm bar.

findings.claim: 'Every arm scored on identical events' — 4848 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them.
findings.problem: Seeing an event is not being scored on it. The declined counts differ by arm (47 for control/placebo/hold-12h/sl-5pct/tp-7pct, 59 for vol-4x, 79 for entry-8pct) and screen_n ranges from 498 to 1563, so the scored populations are not identical across arms. The check establishes shared detection, not the paired population its title claims.

findings.claim: Arm rows report screen_wr and screen_ev as the headline comparison, e.g. sl-5pct screen_wr=55.385 screen_dWR=5.26pp.
findings.problem: These are backfill-tier statistics — events by tier show 4764 backfill vs 84 live — yet they are the only numbers presented with any precision for each arm. No p-value is attached to any screen_dWR against the stated corrected alpha=0.00833, so a 5.26pp delta on n=1560 is displayed as if it were a verdict-grade result while the methodology says only live-tape evidence can promote.

findings.claim: 'Placebo is provably inert' — control n=1560 WR=50.1, placebo n=1560 WR=50.1, discordant pairs b=0 c=0.
findings.problem: The placebo is registered under class=liquidity_filter with min_price=1e-12, while control is class=entry_trigger. A placebo that is byte-identical in outcome to control tests only that a no-op parameter is a no-op; it does not exercise the liquidity_filter path it is registered against, so it cannot detect a bug in the class of arm it is standing in for (vol-4x).

findings.claim: 'Kernel finds the same setups as the live bot' at 219/224 (97.8%), passing the stated 90% bar.
findings.problem: All five listed misses are concentrated in two names (BOME four times, BANANA once) rather than randomly distributed, which is the signature of a systematic kernel disagreement on specific coins, not sampling noise. A pass/fail threshold on an aggregate rate cannot establish agreement when the failures cluster; the concentration is itself evidence of drift on a subpopulation.

findings.claim: 'Corrected bar counts every question asked' — lifetime tests=6, pre-registered hypotheses=6, alpha=0.00833.
findings.problem: The arena lists 7 running arms and 9 retired/screen arms, and the graveyard contains 50 loaded refutations plus multiple L-* screen kills that quote their own alpha (L-sl-entry-anchor cites α=0.01250, implying a 4-test correction). A lifetime count of 6 does not reconcile with the number of arms that have actually been scored and killed, so the correction may be under-counting the questions asked.
